confirmed: Source checked: arXiv:2608.09698v1 [cs.HC], 10 Aug 2026 (PDF p. 1), 14 PDF pages, with UIST 2026 conference metadata and DOI 10.1145/3830398.3830563 on p. 2; the title and seven-author list match the form (pp. 1-2).

Read the entire markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A-C; verified relevant statistics against PDF text and visually checked Figure 5. The included appendices are participant demographics, baseline features, and evaluation reliability (PDF p. 14).
Main study: 12 writers, comprising 8 hobbyists and 4 online novelists; 10 of 12 had prior AI-writing-tool experience (PDF p. 7, Section 5.2; p. 14, Table 2).

The same participants completed both conditions. The main count is 12 people, not the sum of the two arm counts or the number of texts/ratings; Section 6.4 reports 10 of 12 paired comparisons (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 5.1-5.4; p. 10, Section 6.4). n_randomized=null is appropriate because randomization is not reported.

The sample is below the 50-person threshold, so eligibility.core=no and criterion_2_at_least_50_people=not_met remain supported regardless of the unresolved allocation method (PDF p. 7, Section 5.2; p. 14, Table 2).

Both conditions use the same graph-based retrieval and Semantic Frame backend, with generative-AI conversational responses; this is an AI-configuration comparison, not AI-generated versus human-generated output (PDF p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 14, Table 3). Qwen3.5-Flash and BAAI/bge-m3 are named on PDF p. 7, continuation of Section 4.4.

Each writer completed two 30-minute writing sessions, targeting approximately 250-400 words per snippet, in the two historical martial-arts domains; recall took place one week later (PDF p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 8, Sections 5.3-5.4).
Two published authors, external to the participant sample, blindly rated anonymized stories on three 7-point verisimilitude dimensions; the analysis averaged their ratings (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.3).
S1-O1 reported numbers match: domain competence M=4.58 versus 3.58; W=2.5, p=.005, q=.015, r=.818 (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; means also visible in p. 9, Figure 5).
S1-O2 reported numbers match: natural integration M=4.92 versus 4.25; p=.045, q=.065, r=.617; it does not survive FDR correction (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; means also visible in p. 9, Figure 5).
S1-O3 specificity numbers match: M=4.17 versus 3.54; p=.065, q=.065, r=.536 (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; means also visible in p. 9, Figure 5).
Composite numbers match: M=4.56 versus 3.79; p=.005, r=.770; 10 of 12 pairs favor VeriForge, and the composite test is uncorrected (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4; p. 9, Figure 5).

The one-line finding correctly reproduces the participant count, all three sets of expert-rating means, and domain-competence p/q values; only domain competence survives correction among the three dimensions (PDF p. 10, Section 6.4).

The paper uses two-sided paired Wilcoxon tests, reports r=|Z|/sqrt(N_eff), and applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within the three expert dimensions with q<.05 as threshold (PDF p. 8, Section 5.5.4). These r values do not standardize mean differences by an outcome SD.

The expert endpoints are domain grounding/verisimilitude, while CSI is a post-task self-report measure; the delayed paragraph task measures knowledge recall rather than a reported creativity/diversity endpoint (PDF p. 8, Sections 5.5.1-5.5.3; p. 10, Sections 6.2 and 6.4). The form appropriately avoids describing these as direct overall-creativity or across-person diversity scores.

Separate supplemental material is referenced for instruments, scale items, deception details, and statistical details, but it is not included in this PDF; Appendices A-C are included (PDF p. 8, Sections 5.5.3-5.5.4; p. 14).
This is an original system/user-study paper, not a synthesis; null synthesis counts and no pooled estimates are appropriate (PDF pp. 4 and 7-10, Sections 3 and 5-6).
summary: The PDF confirms 12 analyzed writers and every number in the reported results and one-line finding, but it does not establish random assignment. Corrections address the unsupported RCT label, omitted study and outcomes, unsupported pilot-overlap claim, analysis exclusions, and unfinished form fields; core exclusion below 50 people remains correct.
